title: CEO Interview with Lieuwke de Jong of Sweet Atoms
gist: Interview with new Sweet Atoms CEO Lieuwke de Jong: an Australian maker of biomass-derived carbon materials pivoting from battery anodes toward defence, aerospace and, tentatively, semiconductors under a sovereign-supply narrative. It is a promotional, partner-seeking pitch with company-reported performance claims and no disclosed customers or revenue.

insights.claim: Sweet Atoms defines sovereign capability as retaining processing, manufacturing, qualification and value creation locally, not merely access to raw materials, and aims to move Australia up the value chain from raw supply to advanced carbon materials.
insights.speaker: Lieuwke de Jong
insights.so_what: Frames the pitch around the policy-backed onshoring theme rather than product specs; funding appeal depends on government and allied priorities.
insights.quote: Sovereign capability is not only about access to raw materials; it is also about the ability to process, manufacture, qualify, and supply high-value materials locally.
insights.locator: There’s a growing push for sovereign capability

insights.claim: The company cites the United States–Australia critical minerals framework as validation, noting it targets coordinated investment in Australian and US processing and manufacturing capability for defence and advanced technologies.
insights.speaker: Lieuwke de Jong
entities: United States–Australia Framework for Securing of Supply in the Mining and Processing of Critical Minerals and Rare Earths
insights.so_what: Policy tailwind is claimed by the CEO, not evidenced as a contract or funding for Sweet Atoms itself.

insights.claim: The stated plan is an end-to-end sovereign chain (Australian feedstock, local conversion, sovereign-manufactured end uses) that can later be replicated in allied markets using local feedstocks.
insights.speaker: Lieuwke de Jong
insights.so_what: A replicable distributed-manufacturing model is the stated upside, but it is unproven and contingent on first succeeding domestically.
insights.quote: this model can be replicated in allied markets using locally available feedstocks
insights.locator: How can potential customers, feedstock suppliers

insights.claim: Sweet Atoms claims its biomass-derived CleanShift C hard carbon delivers reversible capacity of about 720 mAh/g for lithium and 330 mAh/g for sodium, above conventional benchmarks.
insights.speaker: Lieuwke de Jong
insights.so_what: Company-reported figures with no independent validation or customer named in the interview.
insights.quote: a biomass-derived hard carbon delivering reversible capacity of approximately 720 mAh/g for lithium and 330 mAh/g for sodium

insights.claim: Elastic Diamond, a flexible glassy carbon coating, is claimed to operate up to 2900°C, cut corrosion rates up to tenfold in magnesium-based systems and suppress dendrites in metal-ion batteries.
insights.speaker: Lieuwke de Jong
insights.so_what: Broad claimed applicability from batteries to stealth coatings suggests early-stage breadth over proven commercial traction.

insights.claim: The product line splits into commodity materials (activated and hard carbons) and frontier specialty carbons, with products made from renewable biomass and agricultural waste.
insights.speaker: Lieuwke de Jong
insights.so_what: Commodity versus frontier split hints at a cash-flow base plus a higher-margin option, though no revenue is disclosed.
insights.locator: The company has two materials categories

themes.theme: Semiconductors as an emerging, unproven end market

insights.claim: Semiconductors are described as only an emerging application, with carbon materials pitched for ultra-high-purity filtration, contamination control, thermal management and conductive materials; the company is still seeking partners to find specific problems it can solve.
insights.speaker: Lieuwke de Jong
insights.so_what: Despite appearing on a semiconductor site, the chip exposure is exploratory: no customer, qualification or spec is given.
insights.quote: We see an opportunity to work with industry partners to determine where Sweet Atoms’ carbon platforms can solve specific problems in that ecosystem.
insights.locator: Semiconductors are an emerging application area

insights.claim: Sweet Atoms joined the 12-month Silicon Catalyst ChipStart AU accelerator for network access and says the program helped it validate adjacent deep-tech markets such as defence and aerospace.
insights.speaker: Lieuwke de Jong
insights.so_what: The company is at the stage of buying introductions and commercial strategy help, which signals pre-revenue or early commercial maturity.
insights.locator: Why did you join Silicon Catalyst ChipStart AU

insights.claim: The commercial goal is recurring revenue from long-term customer partnerships, embedded across the full life of customer programs rather than one-off product sales.
insights.speaker: Lieuwke de Jong
insights.so_what: Qualification-driven, sticky supply is attractive if achieved, but the timeline and any existing customers are not stated.
insights.quote: embedded in our customers’ supply chains
